title: Lesson 62 - Optimal Object Design: Standard vs Custom Objects Supporting OmniStudio Artifacts
description: Guide in the creation of a Conceptual Model, Logical Model, and Physical Model to support the business solution, including recommending optimal object design (standard vs. custom) to support Omnistudio artifacts.

questions.question: A business concept is a customer, and the solution needs the standard reporting and integration that come with it. What is the best object choice?
questions.explanation: A customer maps to the standard Account object, which brings the built-in reporting, integration, and familiarity the solution needs. A custom object duplicates the standard one and splits the data. A custom setting and a custom metadata type are for configuration, not for customer records.

questions.question: A business concept, such as a product configuration, has no clean standard object and the standard objects would force compromises. What is the best choice?
options: Force it into a standard object anyway
Create a custom object that matches the requirement
Store it in a custom label
Put it in a custom setting
questions.explanation: When a concept has no clean standard home and standard objects would force compromises, a custom object gives the team the shape it needs without the baggage. Forcing it into a standard object creates workarounds. A custom label and a custom setting are for configuration, not for transactional records.

questions.question: An architect is choosing between a lookup and a master-detail relationship for related records. What should drive the decision?
options: The default, which is always master-detail
The cascade, sharing, and reporting needs of the relationship
The number of fields on the object
questions.explanation: The choice between lookup and master-detail should be driven by the cascade, sharing, and reporting needs, because master-detail cascades deletes and controls access while a lookup is more flexible. The default is not always master-detail. Field count and object name do not determine the relationship type.
